My EDC and "Hopefully Get Home Bag"

-First Aid Kit

-Multi Tool

-Screwdriver set

-Mechanix Gloves

-Folding knife

-Fixed knife

-LED Flashlight (with extra lithium batteries)

-10mAh USB battery pack (for charging phones and other devices)

-Compass

-Map of local area

-Portable Ham radio

-Lighter

-Paracord (was 100ft, I've used a bit of it)

-Water bottle

-Breakfast bars

-.380auto in a hidden compartment (only when I'm not at work)

-Duncan Butterfly Yo-yo

-ethernet cable tester

-various thumbdrives and external hard drives.

jeez, it seems like a lot when I list it all out like that. Some of the stuff comes in handy on the job. The bag carries it pretty well and I don't find its that heavy...probably because I've built it up over time and carry it prettymuch every day. The bag itself is one I got from the local military surplus store. Not too bad for $80. Tons of storage. One of the straps started to fray but I put some superglue on it and it seems to have stopped getting worse.

Some other small that could help, which have almost no weight or volume, and which I often forget:

  • Bags: Garbage, grocery, ziplock. Useful to carry or contain messy things, or protect things (maps, notepads, clothes) from water.

  • Cloths: Bandanas or shop rags for wiping and wrapping. Useful for bloody noses, dusty wind, sweat, and cleaning yourself or your equipment.

  • Velcro: The very cheap green garden tape is easy to tear and faster for small jobs than paracord. The stronger varieties are useful for other light jobs without having to cut or knot, and are wider than string or cord, so they distribute weight better.

  • Chopsticks: Cheap or free, light-weight. Useful for eating crumbly or gelled food with dirty hands, picking up other things indirectly, or as small stakes or pokes.
The folding one is a 4in Kershaw, which is probably one of my favorite knives that I own. The fixed blade is a 4in Ka-bar which is pretty great too.

It sure can get expensive but then again, the way I look at it, most hobbies are expensive. A new set of tires for my jeep are about a grand, a new AR is about a grand, and a decent mobile HF rig is about a grand.

As far as 2m goes, I have nothing but good stuff to say about my Kenwood TM-281 (its a mobile radio but I use it as my base station). I cobbled together a half wave ground plane, mounted it in my attic and I can hit a majority of repeaters within about 60miles. For my truck, I have a quarter wave mag mount that I hook up to the baofeng. Its not great, but it does the job enough. The only reason I'm not gonna get another 281 for my truck is because I want to be able to crossband with whatever radio I put in there.
